Maya: Quick question — we're finalizing Dedicated sizing for the new 70B q4f16 variant in eu-west and us-west. Do we keep the same concurrency targets per GPU or split by region/GPU-type?
Samir: Split. traffic profiles differ and H100 density changes p95. I ran short sims.
Jenn: Can you paste the sim numbers? we need anything that feeds into the quota request.
Samir: pasted results below (synthetic test: seq_len=1024, mix: 60% gen/40% chat). H100 (us-west): p50=85ms p95=230ms throughput=~6200 tok/s per GPU @ concurrency=12. A100 (eu-west): p50=110ms p95=310ms throughput=~4200 tok/s per GPU @ concurrency=8.
Li: Those p95 deltas align with kernel choices — H100 uses fused-attn kernel v3, A100 still on fallback v2 for long seqs. v3 reduces attention cost ~18% for long tokens.
Maya: So for Dedicated pool sizing (throughput target = 1.2e8 tok/day) how many GPUs each region? rough calc pls.
Samir: Quick calc: required sustained tok/s = 1.2e8 / (24*3600) ≈ 1389 tok/s. Add 25% autoscale headroom => 1736 tok/s.
Samir: If we put H100 in us-west: use 6200 tok/s per GPU => 1 GPU suffices nominally, but we need concurrency headroom and rolling updates, so plan 3 GPUs (2 active + 1 buffer) to keep p95 SLAs under spikes.
Samir: For eu-west on A100: 4200 tok/s per GPU => 1736/4200 ≈ 0.42 => still 1 GPU nominal. but given higher p95 and regional burstiness, recommend 2 GPUs (1 active + 1 buffer).
Jenn: That seems optimistic compared to historical peaks. Can we run a 48-hr spike sim @ 2x traffic to validate headroom?
Li: I'm running a sim now with realistic interarrival (bursty): 48h, base=1x, two 10m 5x spikes every 6h. Uploading logs in a sec.
ops-bot: deploy:loadtest/2026-03-18 started by Li — job id load-2101 — ETA ~45m
Li: Quick snippet from run (spike window):
```
[load-2101] target_tps=4200 sustained=8400
GPU-0 (A100) avg_lat_p95=520ms CPU wait increased, queue depth=14
GPU-1 (A100) avg_lat_p95=340ms queue depth=6
Autoscale: added 1 GPU at t+3m, removed at t+25m
```
Samir: Key takeaway: single-A100 pool hit p95>500ms during hot spikes even after autoscale; warmup/add latency ~3m. Warm spare is useful for short spikes.
Maya: So operational policy: set min_replicas=1, warm_spare=1 (pre-warmed), autoscale cooldown=60s, scale_up_target=cpu+queue triggers at 70%. Does that match?
Frank: Add rule: prefer immediate fallback to q2_k_m variant if p95>500ms for >2m to preserve throughput (quality regression acceptable under extreme load).
Jenn: What about kernel rollout? Can A100 run fused-attn v3 with a different cuDNN/driver combo? Risky in private deployments.
Li: We tested v3 on A100 in canary — requires driver 535+ and patched kernel. Performance improved ~12% p95 but regression on small-batch throughput at cold start. Recommend staged rollout: canary in us-west H100 first, then eu-west A100 with rollbacks.
Maya: Can someone summarize final capacity ask for finance + ticket? I need numbers and justification.
Samir: Summary (to use in ticket body):
- Target sustained capacity: 1.2e8 tokens/day global (split by region: 60% us-west, 40% eu-west).
- Autoscale headroom: 25% nominal, plus 1 warm spare per pool for spike absorption.
- Pool plan: us-west (H100) -> 3 GPUs (2 active, 1 warm spare); eu-west (A100) -> 2 GPUs (1 active, 1 warm spare).
- Concurrency targets: H100 concurrency cap=12, A100 concurrency cap=8.
- Autoscale policy: min_replicas=1, warm_spare=1, scale_up when queue>8 or cpu>70%, cooldown=60s.
- Fallback strategy: auto-fallback to q2_k_m model variant when p95>500ms for >2m.
- Kernel rollout: canary v3 on H100 first; test driver 535+ for A100 before wider rollout.
Maya: perfect. Jenn can you put this into the finance ticket and tag infra?
Jenn: On it. I'll open ticket FIN-3842 with the plan and attach sim logs. tagging @infra. :spiral_note_pad: 
Samir: one more note — re-eval after 2 weeks of production telemetry, adjust warm_spare down if sustained stable.
Maya: thanks all :thumbsup:
